memory.keep.note: Decision vocabulary. The product's Accept/Skip are immediate server actions; keep/drop/undecided name a local judgment that is only transmitted on Apply, which is a genuinely different thing.

memory.drop.note: Decision vocabulary, the counterpart to memory.keep. The product's Accept/Skip are immediate server actions; keep/drop/undecided name a local judgment that is only transmitted on Apply.

memory.undecided.note: Decision vocabulary: the third state, a claim the reviewer has not judged yet. The product has no such state — upstream a proposal is pending until an immediate Accept or Skip resolves it.

memory.applying.note: The commit's busy state. The catalog's reviewqueue.accepting ("Accepting...") speaks the server vocabulary, but this button commits a local keep/drop judgment and reads "Apply decided" at rest — the busy state must not switch vocabularies mid-press.

memory.dropped.note: Result of a commit, in the local vocabulary. The catalog's reviewqueue.skipped is "Proposals skipped" — Skip is the product's own immediate server action, while this count is the reviewer's drops the engine confirmed removed. Same number, our word for it.

memory.draftsWillApply.note: Apply-dock forecast. The dock used to say drafts "will be sent", a fourth verb for the commit beside keep/drop and Apply; the catalog only reports per draft after the fact ("Applied") and has no forward-looking phrase to borrow. Counts drafts, not claims.

memory.nearLimit.note: The product ships caps and a binary budget rejection, nothing for approaching one; extended from its "Limits:" label.

memory.overLimit.note: The product ships caps and a binary budget rejection, nothing for approaching one; extended from its "Limits:" label. This is the far side of memory.nearLimit.

memory.restorePoint.note: Restore-point framing over the product's existing backup export. The catalog offers the file operation (exportBackup) but never the pre-flight habit of taking one before a destructive batch.

memory.restorePointDone.note: Restore-point framing over the product's existing backup export; the confirmation half of memory.restorePoint. memorysettings.memoryBackupExported names the file, not the safety net.

memory.facetsComputed.note: Facet-rail provenance heading (the review study's grouping): a facet the console derives itself. The catalog has no facet rail and so nothing that groups fields by where they came from.

memory.facetsFromModel.note: Facet-rail provenance heading (the review study's grouping): a facet the extraction model asserted. See memory.facetsComputed for why the group names are ours.

memory.facetsYours.note: Facet-rail provenance heading (the review study's grouping): a facet the reviewer set by hand. See memory.facetsComputed for why the group names are ours.

memory.autoIncluded.note: Batch reporting: the product reports per draft; we report per batch. Not plural-selected on purpose — the line only renders when the count is two or more, because one dependency is reported inline on its own row.

memory.queueEmpty.note: Empty queue: the product has no string for this state (its own empty state names the Sources screen's condition).

memory.disposition.new.note: Disposition names: schema values the product computes but never labels. The catalog's "New" is a source-status chip in the sources workspace; this is one of a lowercase triad with merge and rewrite, and borrowing a capitalised word for one of three breaks the set.

memory.disposition.merge.note: Disposition names: schema values the product computes but never labels. `merge` folds new material into a memory that already exists.

memory.disposition.rewrite.note: Disposition names: schema values the product computes but never labels. `rewrite` replaces the stored section text instead of adding to it.

memory.nav.vault.note: Navigation label. The catalog names this view in full ("Memory Vault"); the console's own nav uses one word each so the four fit as equal targets on a phone without truncating. Owner's call, 2026-08-22 — the full catalog name still heads the screen.

memory.nav.review.note: The catalog's short navigation label happens to be exactly the one word the console's rail needs; the longer longtermmemorynavigation.reviewQueue still heads the screen itself.

memory.nav.activity.note: Navigation label. The catalog has an activityview namespace but no label for the view — upstream reaches it from a menu the console does not have. One word, per the memory.nav.vault rule.

memory.sourcesPending.note: Sources not yet imported; the catalog counts them but never labels the set. The Sources screen's state vocabulary is otherwise the product's (New / Already imported / Update available / Context changed / Extraction incomplete).

memory.sourcesBlocked.note: Drafts held before review; the catalog says "blocked" only inside sentences and never as a label for the set of them.

memory.sourcesReviewEach.note: The per-kind affordance for sources that must be curated, not bulk-imported. The catalog's verbs here are Import and extract / Re-extract / Select all / Refresh — all bulk, none for opting out of bulk.

memory.extractionText.note: The editable text extraction reads; the override is new to this console. Upstream extraction always reads the source note verbatim, so there is nothing to name.

memory.noMatchingSources.note: The catalog has the whole family — "No matching chats/characters/branches/personas/places" — but not sources, and the Sources search was borrowing the chats one while its own body text said "sources". Same sentence shape, right noun.

memory.zonePreview.note: Detail-pane zone label (v5), anchored to catalog vocabulary: "preview" from reviewqueue.evidenceAndPreview / previewUnavailable, where it only ever appears inside a longer phrase. Lowercase because eyebrows uppercase in CSS.

memory.zoneDiff.note: Detail-pane zone label (v5), built from reviewqueue.existingValue / proposedValue, which are whole interpolated sentences carrying the value. The arrow pairing them as one eyebrow is ours. Lowercase because eyebrows uppercase in CSS.

memory.zoneNewMemory.note: Detail-pane zone label (v5), from reviewqueue.newMemory. Kept lowercase because zone eyebrows uppercase in CSS and this same string also renders in the zone's foot line, which does not — the catalog's title-cased "New memory" would read as a heading there.

memory.zoneExtraction.note: Detail-pane zone label (v5), from the extractiondetails namespace. Lowercase for the same reason as memory.zonePreview; the catalog's "Extraction" is a settings-section heading, which is the one place this word is NOT an eyebrow.

memory.claim.note: The single reviewable item in the queue. The catalog has zero occurrences of "claim" in any key or value: the product's vocabulary is a five-word lifecycle — candidate (at extraction) → proposal / mutation (in review, inside a draft) → suggestion (once rejected) — and none of those five names the thing a reviewer holds one of. The console keeps "claim" because the wire schema already does: `claimKind: "static" | "change"` on interface Mutation (data.ts:40), so an object whose kind is a claimKind is a claim. ClaimDetail.tsx is named for that field and glossary.tsx anchors the term to it. Note "claim kind" itself is domain vocabulary, not a coinage — it names the schema field verbatim. Only the bare noun is ours.

memory.batch.note: The set of claims applied in one go, which may span drafts. Distinct from "draft", which is the container the engine returns claims in and which the catalog does have a word for. The product reports per draft; the console reports per batch, and the catalog has no word for the user's own apply-unit.

memory.section.note: The note sub-part. Unlike everything else here, the product DOES have a word for this and we are deliberately not using it: memoryvault renames the sub-part to "detail" user-visibly (memoryvault.addSection = "Create detail", newSection = "New detail", detailRequired, detailNameExample), so "detail" there really does mean the sub-part, not a detail pane. But the product contradicts itself: reviewqueue still says section (addToSection = "Add to section", updateSection = "Update section", sectionTextCannotBeEmpty). The schema and wire format do not contradict themselves at all — `sections: Record<string, NoteSection>`, mutation kinds `append_section` / `update_section`, `SECTION_CAP` (data.ts). The console keeps "section" because it matches the schema, the wire format, and one of the two product surfaces; memoryvault's "detail" is the outlier. Owner's call — recorded here so the divergence is a decision, not a drift.

memory.existing.note: Diff-zone eyebrow label, rendered on its own as well as inside memory.zoneDiff. Derived from reviewqueue.existingValue ("Existing: {{value}}"), a whole interpolated sentence carrying the value — it cannot be used as a bare label, so the catalog has no string for the label alone. Lowercase because eyebrows uppercase in CSS.

memory.proposed.note: Diff-zone eyebrow label, rendered on its own as well as inside memory.zoneDiff. Derived from reviewqueue.proposedValue ("Proposed: {{value}}"), a whole interpolated sentence carrying the value — it cannot be used as a bare label, so the catalog has no string for the label alone. Lowercase because eyebrows uppercase in CSS.
